elements.details:
Four line charts labeled A, B, C, and D showing CO2 emissions in millions of metric tonnes over time.

Graph A: Timeline 1800-2050, CO2 range 0-100,000 million metric tonnes. Shows a slow increase from 1800 to about 1950, then a sharp rise peaking around 2000-2010 near 8,000 million metric tonnes, then a slight decline.

Graph B: Timeline 1980-2030, CO2 range 0-7,000 million metric tonnes. Shows a rise from about 4,500 in 1980 to a peak near 6,000 around 2005, then a decline to about 5,000 by 2020.

Graph C: Timeline 1800-2050, CO2 range 0-7,000 million metric tonnes. Shows near zero until 1900, then a steady rise with fluctuations, peaking near 6,500 around 2000, then declining slightly.

Graph D: Timeline 1900-2000, CO2 range 0-5,000 million metric tonnes. Shows steady increase from about 500 in 1900 to 5,000 near 1980-2000 with some fluctuations.

All graphs have x-axis labeled 'Timeline' and y-axis labeled 'CO2 (Millions of Metric Tonnes)'. No legend or units beyond metric tonnes. Trends show overall increase in CO2 emissions over time with recent peaks and some declines.
elements.summary: Figure 8.11 presents four line graphs (A-D) depicting CO2 emissions over different time spans and scales, illustrating historical trends and recent changes in greenhouse gas emissions.
